## From Prototype to Production

### Why This Week Matters

- **Demos are easy, production is hard**: the gap is evals + observability
- **Non-determinism**: same input, different outputs — traditional QA breaks down
- **Silent failures**: LLM apps degrade without throwing exceptions
- **Trust**: you cannot ship what you cannot measure or monitor

## Evaluation: Why Evaluate?

### The Case for Systematic Evals

- **Quality assurance**: measuring model and application performance
- **Regression detection**: catch degradation when you swap models or edit prompts
- **Comparison**: selecting the best model, prompt, or pipeline variant
- **Compliance**: demonstrating requirements are met
- **Continuous improvement**: evals turn vibes into engineering

## Evaluation Metrics

### What to Measure

- **Accuracy / correctness**: is the output right?
- **Relevance**: does it answer the actual question?
- **Faithfulness / groundedness**: is it supported by the provided context?
- **Consistency**: reproducible results across runs
- **Safety**: adherence to guardrails and policy
- **Latency and cost**: operational quality is part of quality

## LLM-as-a-Judge

### Using Models to Grade Models

- **Idea**: a strong LLM scores outputs against a rubric
- **Modes**: pointwise scoring, pairwise comparison, reference-based grading
- **Strengths**: scalable, cheap relative to humans, works on open-ended text
- **Known biases**: position bias, verbosity bias, self-preference
- **Mitigations**: randomize order, use rubrics, calibrate against human labels

## Designing Good Judge Prompts

### Rubrics Over Vibes

- Define explicit criteria and a bounded score scale
- Provide few-shot graded examples to anchor the scale
- Ask for reasoning **before** the score (structured output)
- Validate the judge itself: measure agreement with human annotations
- Keep judges pinned to a model version for reproducibility

## RAG Evaluation

### Evaluating Retrieval and Generation Separately

- **Retrieval metrics**: context precision, context recall, hit rate, MRR
- **Generation metrics**: faithfulness (grounded in retrieved context), answer relevance
- **End-to-end**: answer correctness against a golden dataset
- **Key insight**: most RAG failures are retrieval failures — measure the stages independently

## RAG Evaluation Tools

### Frameworks

- **RAGAS**: RAG assessment framework — faithfulness, context precision/recall
- **DeepEval**: pytest-style LLM evaluation library
- **TruLens**: feedback functions and the "RAG triad"
- **Phoenix (Arize)**: evals plus tracing in one tool
- Golden datasets: start small (50–100 curated examples), grow from production

## Agent Evaluation

### Beyond Single-Turn Quality

- Agents produce **trajectories**, not just answers
- **Outcome evals**: did the agent complete the task?
- **Trajectory evals**: did it take reasonable steps? Correct tool selection, tool-call arguments, no loops
- **Efficiency**: steps taken, tokens burned, wall-clock time
- **Failure taxonomy**: wrong tool, bad arguments, premature stop, infinite loop, hallucinated tool output

## Trajectory Evaluation in Practice

### Techniques

- Compare trajectories against reference paths (exact, in-order, any-order matching)
- LLM-as-a-judge over the full trace: "was each step justified?"
- Unit-test individual tools deterministically; eval the planner separately
- Replay production traces as regression suites

## Human Evaluation

### Still the Gold Standard

- **Annotation guidelines**: clear, written criteria
- **Inter-annotator agreement**: consistency checks before trusting labels
- **A/B testing**: comparing variants on live traffic
- **Feedback loops**: thumbs up/down, edit-distance from accepted answers
- Use humans to calibrate automated judges, then scale with automation

## Observability Fundamentals

### What is Observability?

- **Definition**: understanding system behavior from its outputs
- **Three pillars**:
  - Metrics: quantitative measurements
  - Logs: detailed event records
  - Traces: request flow tracking
- GenAI adds a fourth concern: **the content itself** (prompts, completions, tool calls)

## Why LLM Apps Need Special Observability

### GenAI-Specific Signals

- **Token usage**: the cost driver — input, output, cached tokens
- **Latency breakdown**: time-to-first-token vs. total generation time
- **Prompt/completion capture**: you must see what the model saw
- **Tool call traces**: agent steps as spans
- **Quality signals**: user feedback, judge scores attached to traces

## Distributed Tracing for GenAI

### Traces and Spans

- **Trace**: one user request end-to-end
- **Spans**: retrieval call, LLM call, tool execution, guardrail check
- **Span attributes**: model name, token counts, temperature, finish reason
- **Bottleneck identification**: which span dominates latency?
- Agent runs become trees of spans — essential for debugging multi-step failures

## OpenTelemetry GenAI Conventions

### An Emerging Standard

- OpenTelemetry defines **semantic conventions for GenAI**: standardized span/attribute names for model calls (`gen_ai.*` attributes)
- Captures: system (provider), model, token usage, prompt/completion events
- Benefit: vendor-neutral instrumentation — switch backends without re-instrumenting
- Supported by a growing ecosystem of LLM observability platforms

## Observability Tools

### The Landscape

- **Langfuse**: open-source LLM engineering platform — traces, evals, prompt management
- **Phoenix / Arize**: tracing plus evaluation
- **LangSmith**: tracing and datasets for LangChain-based (and other) apps
- **Weights & Biases Weave**: experiment tracking extended to LLM apps
- **OpenTelemetry + your existing APM**: reuse infrastructure you already run

## Logging Best Practices

### Structured Logging

- **JSON logging**: machine-readable events
- **Context enrichment**: request IDs, user/session IDs, model versions
- **Log levels**: appropriate use of DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
- **Sensitive data**: redact PII and secrets **before** they hit logs
- Link logs to traces via trace IDs

## Continuous Evaluation in Production

### Online Evaluation

- **Online evals**: score a sample of live traffic with judges
- **A/B testing**: compare model/prompt versions on real users
- **Drift detection**: input distribution shifts over time
- **Alerting**: automated detection of quality or cost regressions
- Production traces become tomorrow's eval datasets

## Guardrails: Why?

### Motivation

- **Risk mitigation**: preventing harmful or off-policy outputs
- **Security**: LLM apps are a new attack surface
- **Compliance**: meeting regulatory and organizational requirements
- **Trust building**: user confidence in AI systems
- Guardrails complement — never replace — good evals

## Guardrail Architecture

### Where Checks Live

- **Input guardrails**: run before the model — topic filters, injection detection, PII scrubbing
- **Output guardrails**: run after the model — toxicity, grounding, format validation
- **In-loop guardrails**: constrain tool use and agent actions
- Tradeoff: every guardrail adds latency and cost — run checks in parallel where possible

## Content Safety Guardrails

### Types

- **Toxicity detection**: filtering harmful content
- **Topic control**: keeping the app on its intended domain
- **PII protection**: detect and redact names, emails, SSNs, account numbers
- **Bias mitigation**: reducing unfair outputs
- **Hallucination checks**: grounding validation against retrieved context

## Prompt Injection

### The #1 LLM Security Risk

- **Direct injection**: user instructs the model to ignore its system prompt
- **Indirect injection**: malicious instructions hidden in retrieved documents, web pages, or tool outputs
- Listed as LLM01 in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
- Agents raise the stakes: injected instructions can trigger real tool actions

## Prompt Injection Defenses

### Defense in Depth

- **Privilege separation**: the model gets least-privilege tool access
- **Input classifiers**: detect injection attempts before the model
- **Instruction hierarchy**: system > developer > user > retrieved content
- **Output validation**: never execute model output without checks
- **Human-in-the-loop**: confirmation gates for irreversible actions
- Accept reality: no defense is complete — design for containment

## Guardrail Tools and Frameworks

### Implementation Options

- **Amazon Bedrock Guardrails**: managed content filtering, PII, grounding checks
- **NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails**: open-source programmable rails
- **Llama Guard**: Meta's open safety classifier models
- **Guardrails AI**: output validation and structured-output enforcement
- **Custom filters**: regex + classifiers for domain-specific policies

## Data Security

### Protecting Sensitive Information

- **Input sanitization**: cleaning user inputs before they reach models
- **Output filtering**: removing sensitive data from responses
- **Access controls**: role-based permissions on data sources and tools
- **Audit logging**: tracking who accessed what through the model
- **Data residency**: where do prompts go? Provider retention policies matter

## Putting It Together

### The Reliability Stack

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Input Guardrails] --> B[LLM / Agent]
    B --> C[Output Guardrails]
    B -.traces.-> D[Observability]
    D -.datasets.-> E[Evals]
    E -.regressions.-> B
```

- Guardrails protect the request path
- Observability captures what happened
- Evals close the loop and drive improvement

### Evals, Tracing, and Guardrails

- Instrument a RAG/agent app with Langfuse tracing
- Build an eval dataset and run LLM-as-a-judge scoring
- Add input/output guardrails (PII + injection checks)
